tests.procedure: Under strong white light, check each received sample container separately in clean, transparent watch glass or glass dish to detect any foreign particles, conformance of colour & compliance with the visual specifications.

details.bp_spec: White or almost white, crystalline powder or colorless crystals.
details.usp_spec: White crystals or crystalline powder, usually having a slight, characteristic odor.
details.reference: USP 2024 Description and Relative Solubility; BP 2024 (SC IV K.) Characters Section in Monographs (Hygroscopicity and Solubility)

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg of powdered sample in a stoppered tube. Add 0.1 ml of solvent, shake vigorously for 1 min, place at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min; if not dissolved repeat shake/hold once (very soluble if dissolved); stepwise add 0.9 mL (freely soluble), 2 mL (soluble), 7 mL (sparingly soluble); if still undissolved, test 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble), then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with specified solvents.

solventsUSP: insoluble in ether and in benzene
details.reference: USP 2024 Description and Relative Solubility; BP 2024 (SC IV K.) Characters Section in Monographs

tests.procedure: Dry test samples at 105 °C for 2 h. Mix intimately with potassium bromide and compress into a transparent pellet. Examine the spectrum obtained for the sample and compare to the spectrum obtained from Thiamine Hydrochloride RS.

details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix II A. Infrared Spectrophotometry; USP 2024 Monograph for Thiamine Hydrochloride

tests.procedure: Identification by fluorescence (BP): Dissolve about 20 mg of sample in 10 mL water, add 1 mL dilute acetic acid and 1.6 mL 1 M NaOH, heat in water-bath for 30 min, allow to cool; add 5 mL dilute NaOH, 10 mL potassium ferricyanide solution and 10 mL butanol, shake vigorously for 2 min. Upper layer shows intense light-blue fluorescence (especially UV 365 nm). Repeat using 0.9 mL 1 M NaOH and 0.1 g anhydrous sodium sulfite instead of 1.6 mL 1 M NaOH: practically no fluorescence is seen.

details.negativeControlReagents: 0.9 mL 1 M sodium hydroxide and 0.1 g anhydrous sodium sulfite

tests.procedure: Chloride identification (USP / BP): Add 1 drop diluted nitric acid and 0.5 mL silver nitrate TS to a 20-mg/mL solution containing about 2 mg chloride ion in 2 mL: white curdy precipitate is formed. Centrifuge without delay, decant supernatant layer, wash precipitate with three 1-mL portions of nitric acid solution (1 in 100), discard washings. Add ammonia TS dropwise to precipitate: dissolves readily.

details.reference: USP 2024 <191>; BP 2024 Appendix VII Limit Tests

tests.procedure: Appearance of solution (BP): Dilute 2.5 mL of solution S to 5 mL with water. Check appearance and compare with reference solution Y7 or GY7.

details.solutionS: 2.5 g in carbon dioxide-free water to 25 mL
details.dilution: 2.5 mL solution S to 5 mL with water
details.expected: The solution is clear and not more intensely colored than reference solution Y7 or GY7
details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix IV A. Clarity of Solution & Appendix IV B. Color of Solution

tests.procedure: Measure the pH of the prepared solution (dilute 2.5 mL solution S to 10 mL with water, or dissolve 1 g sample in 100 mL water) with a calibrated pH meter.

details.samplePrep: dilute 2.5 mL of solution S to 10 mL with water or dissolve 1 gm of sample in 100 mL of water
details.reference: USP 2024 Monograph for Thiamine Hydrochloride; BP 2024 Monograph for Thiamine Hydrochloride

tests.procedure: Determine the water content using Karl Fischer titrator on 400 mg sample.

details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix IX C. Determination of Water; USP 2024 <921> Water Determination

tests.procedure: Limit of nitrate (USP): Dissolve 40 mg sample in 2 mL water, add 2 mL sulfuric acid, cool, and superimpose 2 mL ferrous sulfate TS. Check for brown ring at junction of layers.

details.observation: No brown ring is produced at the junction of the two layers

tests.procedure: Absorbance of solution (USP): Prepare 100 mg/mL solution in water of the test sample. Filter through syringe filter or fine-porosity, sintered-glass funnel. Determine absorbance of sample solution against water blank at 400 nm in a 1-cm cell.

details.filtration: syringe filter or fine-porosity sintered-glass funnel

tests.procedure: Accurately weigh empty crucible previously ignited at 600-650 °C and cooled in desiccator (W0). Weigh accurately 1.0 g sample into platinum crucible (W1 = empty plate weight + material weight). Moisten with small amount of sulfuric acid (usually 1 mL). Heat gently on hot plate until thoroughly charred. After cooling, moisten residue with sulfuric acid, heat until white fumes cease. Ignite in muffle furnace at 600-650 °C to constant weight, cool in desiccator, weigh (W2). % Residue on ignition / sulfated ash = ((W2 - W0) / (W1 - W0)) x 100.

details.reference: USP 2024 <281>; BP 2024 Appendix IX A. Determination of Sulfated Ash

tests.procedure: Sulfates limit test (BP): Sample solution: dilute 5 mL solution S to 15 mL with distilled water. Suspension: add 3 mL of 250 g/L barium chloride to 4.5 mL sulfate standard solution (10 ppm SO4) R1, shake, stand 1 min. To 2.5 mL of this suspension add 15 mL sample solution and 0.5 mL acetic acid. Standard: to 2.5 mL suspension add 15 mL sulfate standard (10 ppm SO4) and 0.5 mL acetic acid. After 5 min, any opalescence in test is not more intense than standard.

details.sampleDilution: 5 mL solution S to 15 mL distilled water
details.suspension: 3 mL of 250 g/L barium chloride + 4.5 mL sulfate standard (10 ppm SO4) R1, stand 1 min
details.testMix: 2.5 mL suspension + 15 mL diluted sample + 0.5 mL acetic acid
details.standardMix: 2.5 mL suspension + 15 mL sulfate standard (10 ppm SO4) + 0.5 mL acetic acid

tests.procedure: Assay (BP, potentiometry): Dissolve 0.110 g sample in 5 mL anhydrous formic acid, add 50 mL acetic anhydride. Titrate within 2 min with 0.1 M perchloric acid, determining endpoint potentiometrically. Carry out blank titration. Assay % = ((E.P sample - E.P blank) x Eq.wt x F / Wt) x 100; Eq.wt = 16.86 mg, F = titrant factor, Wt = corrected weight of sample considering moisture content.

details.solvents: 5 mL anhydrous formic acid + 50 mL acetic anhydride
details.equivalenceFactor: each mL of 0.1 M perchloric acid is equivalent to 16.86 mg thiamine hydrochloride
details.formula: Assay % = ((E.P_sample - E.P_blank) x Eq.wt x F / Wt) x 100
details.titrantPreparation: 0.1 M perchloric acid VS: 8.5 mL perchloric acid in about 900 mL glacial acetic acid, add 30 mL acetic anhydride, to 1000.0 mL with glacial acetic acid, stand 24 h
details.titrantStandardization: 0.170 g potassium hydrogen phthalate in 50 mL anhydrous acetic acid (warm gently if needed), cool protected from air, titrate with perchloric acid solution using 0.05 mL crystal violet solution

tests.source: Thiamine Hydrochloride__STM-003 Thiamine Hydrochloride.txt:39; titrant STM-003:26

tests.procedure: Assay (USP, HPLC with internal standard): Mobile phase: Solution A (0.005 M sodium 1-octanesulfonate in 1 in 100 glacial acetic acid) and Solution B (methanol:acetonitrile 3:2) 60:40. Internal standard: 2.0% (v/v) methyl benzoate in methanol. Standard: 20.0 mL of 1-mg/mL Thiamine HCl RS in mobile phase + 5.0 mL IS diluted to 50 mL (400 µg/mL). Sample: 10.0 mL of 2-mg/mL Thiamine HCl in mobile phase + 5.0 mL IS diluted to 50 mL (400 µg/mL). Column: 4-mm x 30-cm, packing L1. Detector: UV 254 nm. Flow rate: 1 mL/min. Injection: 10 µL. Result = (RU/RS) x (CS/CU) x 100.

details.solutionA: 0.005 M sodium 1-octanesulfonate in dilute glacial acetic acid (1 in 100)
details.standardSolution: 400 µg/mL thiamine hydrochloride RS + 0.2% methyl benzoate in mobile phase
details.sampleSolution: 400 µg/mL thiamine hydrochloride + 0.2% methyl benzoate in mobile phase

systemSuitability.resolution: NLT 4.0 between thiamine and methyl benzoate peaks
systemSuitability.columnEfficiency: NLT 1500 theoretical plates for thiamine peak
systemSuitability.rsd: NMT 2.0% for ratios of thiamine peak area to internal standard peak area

details.reference: USP 2024 Monograph for Thiamine Hydrochloride; USP <621>

tests.procedure: Related compounds (USP, HPLC): Sample solution: 1.0 mg/mL Thiamine Hydrochloride in mobile phase. Column: 4.0-mm x 15-cm, packing L1. Detector: UV 254 nm. Flow rate: 0.75 mL/min. Injection: 10 µL. Allow sample to elute for NLT 3 times retention time of main peak. Result % = (rU/rT) x 100; rU = sum of areas of all peaks except thiamine; rT = sum of areas of all peaks.

details.runtime: NLT 3 times retention time of main peak
details.reference: USP 2024 Monograph for Thiamine Hydrochloride; USP <621>

tests.procedure: Related substances (BP, gradient HPLC): Test solution: 0.35 g in 15.0 mL 5% V/V glacial acetic acid, dilute to 100.0 mL with water. Ref (a): thiamine for system suitability CRS (impurities A, B, C) in 1 mL 0.75% V/V glacial acetic acid. Ref (b): test solution diluted 1:100 then 1:10 with water. Column: 250 x 4.0 mm, end-capped octadecylsilyl silica gel (5 µm), 45 °C. Mobile phase A: 3.764 g/L sodium hexanesulfonate pH 3.1 with H3PO4; B: methanol. Gradient: 0-2 min 10% B; 2-27 min 10->30% B; 27-35 min 30->50% B; 35-42 min 50% B. Flow rate: 1.0 mL/min. UV 248 nm. Injection: 25 µL.

details.column: 250 mm x 4.0 mm, end-capped octadecylsilyl silica gel (5 µm)
details.mobilePhaseA: 3.764 g/L sodium hexanesulfonate adjusted to pH 3.1 with phosphoric acid R
details.calculation: for each impurity, use concentration of thiamine in reference solution (b); reporting threshold 0.05%
details.reference: BP 2024 Monograph for Thiamine Hydrochloride; BP Appendix III D

openQuestions.question: BP assay calculation unit inconsistency: The formula is stated as ((E.P sample - E.P blank) x Eq.wt x F / Wt) x 100 with Eq.wt = 16.86 mg and sample weight 0.110 g. If Wt is entered in grams (0.110 g), the formula produces a result off by a factor of 1000 unless Wt is in mg (110 mg) or Eq.wt is converted to 0.01686 g. Row transcribed as written; confirm Wt unit.

USP HPLC assay anhydrous basis correction: The USP specification requires 98.0%-102.0% on an anhydrous basis, but the calculation formula in STM line 38 (Result = (RU/RS) x (CS/CU) x 100) does not include a moisture correction factor 100 / (100 - Water%) or specify pre-drying the sample. Confirm whether anhydrous correction is applied during calculation.

openQuestions.question: Microbiology procedures absent from STM: Both BP and USP specification sheets specify TAMC (NMT 10^3 CFU/gm), TYMC (NMT 10^2 CFU/gm), and E. coli (Absent / 10gm), but STM-003 contains only physicochemical testing procedures. Microbiology tests are handled per general SOP C2I-91-128.
